Manure Management Systems: Configuration Guide

Manure.Rmd

Introduction & Purpose

In herdr, manure methane (CH4CH_4) and direct/indirect nitrous oxide (N2ON_2O) emissions are governed by the systems declared in user_data/manure_management.csv.

To ensure IPCC Tier 2 compliance, the values entered must match official IPCC system definitions and climate combinations recorded in ipcc_mm.csv. If an invalid combination is entered, the model cannot assign emission factors.

This guide provides the complete decision matrix of valid paths for your manure_management.csv. For the mathematical emission equations, see the Theoretical Basis.

1. The Two Fundamental Rules

Rule 1: Allocation Must Equal Exactly 1.0 per Cohort

For each unique animal cohort (defined by animal_tag, region, subregion, and class_flex), the sum of the allocation column across all assigned manure systems must equal 1.0 (100%):

∑allocation=1.0\sum \text{allocation} = 1.0

Example: If dairy cows spend 7 months indoors with liquid slurry and 5 months grazing on pasture, declare two rows for that cohort: * Row 1: system_base = "liquid_slurry", allocation = 0.583 (7/127 / 12). * Row 2: system_base = "pasture_range_paddock", allocation = 0.417 (5/125 / 12).

Rule 2: Strict Lowercase Identifiers

All system descriptors, variants, and climate zones are strictly lowercase (e.g., zone_dry, NOT Zone_Dry).

2. High-Detail Systems (Storage Duration Dependent)

For slurry, pits, and lagoons, Methane Conversion Factors (MCFMCF) depend directly on how many months manure is stored and the regional temperature/moisture profile.

3. Standard Systems (Climate-Only)

For standard solid, composting, digestion, and grazing systems, sub-climates, storage months, and climate zones are not required. Leave those columns blank.

4. Climate & Moisture Definitions

Temperature Classification (system_climate):

  • cool: Mean annual temperature (MAT) <15∘C< 15^\circ\text{C} (e.g., Northern and Atlantic Spain, Central and Northern Europe).
  • temperate: MAT between 15∘C15^\circ\text{C} and 25∘C25^\circ\text{C} (e.g., Mediterranean basin, Southern Spain).
  • warm: MAT >25∘C> 25^\circ\text{C} (e.g., tropical lowlands).

Moisture Classification (climate_moisture):

  • For High-Detail Systems: Align with climate_zone:
    • If zone_wet, zone_moist, or zone_montane →\rightarrow use wet.
    • If zone_dry →\rightarrow use dry.
  • For Standard Systems: Use default.
